levels.title: Sort the rules

items.text: Indication requires a candle close through the PIL
Entry at the first valid retest
Continuation must close back through the PIL

levels.name: Strategy or personal?
levels.brief: Not “what would a disciplined trader do?”. What does YOUR rulebook say?

options.text: I won’t chase unless it looks really good.
options.feedback: BUILT-IN LOOPHOLE: “unless it looks really good”.

options.text: If my retest entry is missed and price moves away, I do not market-enter late. I wait for a new valid setup.

slide.title: Two losses today. A valid setup forms.
High-impact event in 4 minutes. Valid setup.
Tight consolidation. A technical setup appears.

thoughts: “Just give it a little more room.”

options.label: Move the stop down. Give it room.

say: −2R. The stop you moved was the only thing between you and this.

options.label: Move the stop down (and this time it comes back)

say: This is the most dangerous outcome in this lesson.
Now your stop is a suggestion. The day it doesn’t come back, there’s no floor.

options.label: Let the stop do its job

say: −1R. Exactly what you planned to risk.
Your limit missed by one tick. Price is leaving.

choice.prompt: Price is +26 from your level. What do you do?

say: It came back to where your limit was. Through your new stop.
The trade you planned had a stop. The trade you chased had a worse one.

options.label: Let it go. Mark it MISSED ACCORDING TO PLAN.

say: A wick through the PIL. No close.
“Basically” isn’t in your model. It’s in your mood.
This time it closed, retested, and became the trade.
Some days it never closes. Either way, the rule decided, not the look.

options.label: The setup quality
options.feedback: The setup didn’t change. Your state did.

options.label: FOMO after a missed opportunity
options.why: The missed winner is the trigger. The chase is the behavior.

options.label: News
options.feedback: Nothing in the sequence points to news.

levels.title: After a loss: the urge to size up

options.label: Next valid trade stays standard planned size, if session rules permit
options.why: Same size. Same rules. The loss doesn’t change the risk model.

options.label: Skip every trade for a week
options.feedback: That’s a feeling, not a rule.

levels.name: Build the response

levels.title: Your rulebook, your session

slide.title: Your rulebook, loaded
slide.body: Session Mode: read-only. If you want to change a rule, flag it for review. Try it if you like.

checkpoints.prompt: First valid retest. Your rules allow a first trade.

slide.title: The retest came and went. Price is running.
“My two-trade maximum might be too restrictive.”

asks.prompt: What do you do with that thought during the session?

options.label: Change the rule now
options.feedback: Rules are read-only in Session Mode.

options.label: Flag it: REVIEW THIS RULE LATER
options.why: Queued. You’ll see it after the session.

slide.title: Daily stop reached. Then: the cleanest setup of the session.

levels.reviewClean: The method, the account and YOUR predefined rules outranked FOMO, revenge, boredom and real-time excuses.
levels.name: FINAL BOSS: Can you follow your own rulebook?

questionBank.question: Valid setup. Daily stop reached. What’s true?
questionBank.why: Setup validity and participation eligibility are separate.

questionBank.question: Invalid setup. Every personal rule is clear. What do you do?
questionBank.why: Personal eligibility can never make an invalid setup valid.

questionBank.question: Missed retest. Price runs to the target. You didn’t chase. Grade it.
questionBank.why: Following the no-chase rule doesn’t require the market to punish the skipped trade.

questionBank.question: Max trades = 2. Two trades done. The third setup is perfect. What does the session rule say?
Mid-session you believe your max should be 3. What do you do?
options: Queue it for review, don’t change it live
questionBank.why: Rules change in Review Mode, with evidence.

questionBank.question: High-impact event in 3 minutes. Your saved rule prohibits entries within 5. Valid setup. Decision?
questionBank.why: Your rule blocks new entries in that window.

questionBank.question: High-impact event in 3 minutes. You have NO news rule defined. What happens?
options: Flag it: NEWS RESPONSE NOT DEFINED
questionBank.why: Undefined is flagged and resolved in Review Mode. Never invented.

questionBank.question: Trade wins. You entered before Continuation. How is it recorded?
questionBank.why: Outcome and adherence are separate dimensions.

questionBank.question: Trade loses. Every rule was followed. How is it recorded?
questionBank.why: A loss is not automatically a mistake.

questionBank.question: You chased after missing a winner. What should the violation review connect?
options: Trigger: missed winner → behavior: chase → your IF / THEN response
questionBank.why: IF trigger X happens, THEN I do Y.

questionBank.question: “I won’t chase unless it looks really good.” What’s the problem?
options: It needs a number of trades
questionBank.why: “Unless it looks really good” is exactly where live-trading-you escapes.

questionBank.question: A personal behavior rule says “after a loss I size up”. Your risk limit is 1R. Which wins?
questionBank.why: A personal rule can never override account safety.

questionBank.question: All technical criteria are met, but your environment rule blocks tight consolidation. Decision?
options: Valid setup · PASS under your plan
questionBank.why: Technically valid can still be outside your participation rules.

questionBank.question: You’re calm and confident. The setup is invalid. Decision?
questionBank.why: Feeling ready doesn’t create technical validity.
